name: misty step
lore:
# The Art of the Silvered Leap: Misty Step

To the uninitiated, *Misty Step* appears as a mere trick of the light. Yet, to the practitioner, it is a sublime folding of the Weave. Upon the final incantation, the caster is instantly enveloped in a swirling shroud of silver-grey vapor. The sensation is akin to a brief, icy plunge into a mountain spring—a momentary weightlessness as the physical form is translated across the threshold of the Ethereal.

### The Weaver’s Touch
When shaping this spell, one feels the Weave thin and turn cold. It requires a sharp, rhythmic pulse of will; you do not walk to your destination, you simply *become* there, leaving behind a faint scent of rain and ozone.

### The Legend of Vaelin
Loremasters attribute the spell’s discovery to Vaelin of the High Reaches, an Elven pathfinder cornered by a displacer beast atop a crumbling precipice. Refusing to fall, Vaelin envisioned himself as the morning fog that clung to the cliffs. When the beast lunged, it passed through nothing but cold steam. Vaelin reappeared thirty paces away, bow drawn, his feet dry and his spirit untethered.
